title: Sourdough starter peak, dense loaf and shorter bulk
description: User's starter peaks in five hours at 26°C; Dorothy covered spotting peak, an underproofed loaf and shorter bulk, plus a quick espresso descaling aside.
abstract: The user's sourdough starter now doubles reliably, first in six hours and later peaking in five hours at 26°C, so the revival is working. Dorothy explained peak signs: domed top just dimpling (concave means past peak), many bubbles, sweet tangy smell, jiggly stringy texture, and a not-foolproof float test; she suggested a rubber band at the starting level. The last loaf was dense and gummy; she said it was most likely underproofed, probably from a weak starter, and advised using it at peak and judging bulk by the dough (up 50-75%, domed, bubbly) at 24-27°C. Asked about shortening bulk, she said probably yes: at 26°C with about 20% starter, bulk often takes 4-6 hours, so check from 3.5-4 hours. The user then asked about descaling an espresso machine: every 2-3 months with hard water, 3-6 with soft, citric acid descaler, no vinegar, rinse well. The user keeps asking for brief answers. Open: whether the next loaf improves; espresso machine model and water hardness.
